cases.derivation: Header 4d546864 00000006 0001 0002 03c0: format 1, two tracks, 960 PPQ. Conductor (19 bytes): 00 ff5804 04 02 18 08 is 4/4 (dd 2 = 2^2; cc 24 = 96/4, one click per quarter; bb 8), 00 ff5103 07a120 is 500000 us, 00 ff2f00. Melody (13 bytes): 00 90 3c 64 is note-on C4 (60) velocity 100 at 0; 87 40 is delta 960 (7 x 128 + 64); 80 3c 40 is its note-off with release velocity 64; 00 ff2f00.
cases.name: one note at 120 BPM in 4/4

cases.derivation: Header and conductor as in the one-note case. Melody (23 bytes): the first delta is 2880 (22 x 128 + 64 = 96 40), so nothing moves to tick 0: 90 43 5a is G4 (67) velocity 90 on beat 4; 87 40 80 43 40 ends it at 3840; at 3840 the note-off comes before 00 90 48 64, C5 (72) velocity 100 on the downbeat; 8f 00 (15 x 128) 80 48 40 ends it at 5760; 00 ff2f00.
cases.name: a pickup on beat 4 keeps its leading rest

cases.derivation: Conductor (54 bytes), meter then tempo then markers at each tick: at 0, 4/4, 07a120 and ff06 05 'verse' (76 65 72 73 65); delta 3840 (30 x 128 = 9e 00), then ff5804 03 02 18 08 (3/4, a click per quarter), 600000 us (0927c0) and ff06 06 'chorus' (63 68 6f 72 75 73). Melody (31 bytes): E4 (64 = 40) velocity 96 (60) at 0 and again at 1920, the first note-off (8f 00 80 40 40) written before the second note-on, so the touching notes stay two; G4 (43) velocity 110 (6e) at 3840 for a dotted half, 2880 (96 40); 00 ff2f00.
cases.name: tempo and meter change with section markers

cases.derivation: The record's tempo map and its one note equal the one-note case; its ids, revisions, corrected origin, confidence, key, phrase, quantize layer and source are MelodySpec-only, so the bytes are the one-note bytes.
cases.name: a whole MelodySpec record writes only its MIDI fields

cases.derivation: Format 0, one track, 480 PPQ (01e0), so every tick doubles exactly. 90 3c 50: C4 velocity 80 at 0; 83 60 (480) 3c 00 is running status 90 with velocity 0, a note-off; 00 3e 50 starts D4 (62) at 480; 83 60 3e 00 ends it at 960. No tempo or time signature, so the SMF defaults hold: 500000 us (120 BPM) and 4/4. At 960 PPQ the notes are 0 + 960 and 960 + 960.
cases.name: format 0 at 480 PPQ with running status and the SMF defaults

cases.derivation: Track 0 (46 bytes): ff03 04 'lead' (a track name), 3/4, ff59 02 00 00 (C major key signature), ff06 07 'Verse 1' (56 65 72 73 65 20 31, not a section name) and ff06 05 'intro' (69 6e 74 72 6f, a section name, so a marker). Track 1 (40 bytes): SysEx f0 05 7e 7f 09 01 f7, the same 3/4 again (one meter entry), program change c0 00, controller b0 07 64, a note-off 80 3c 40 with no note sounding, then C4 velocity 100 from 0 to 960 (87 40). Only the note, the meter and 'intro' are carried; each other event is listed by track, tick and status (ff and the meta type for meta events). No tempo event: the SMF default 500000 us.
cases.name: events a MelodySpec does not carry are listed, never dropped

cases.derivation: Division e728 has its top bit set: SMPTE timing (e7 = -25 frames per second, 28 = 40 ticks per frame), which has no ticks per quarter note, so no 960 PPQ tempo map exists for it.
cases.name: SMPTE time division

cases.derivation: ff51 03 00 00 00 sets 0 us per quarter; the tempo map holds integers from 1 to 16777215.
cases.name: a tempo of 0 us per quarter

cases.derivation: nn 21 is 33 beats; a MelodySpec meter has at most 32.
cases.name: a 33/4 time signature

cases.derivation: dd 06 is a denominator of 2^6 = 64; a MelodySpec meter stops at 32.
cases.name: a 4/64 time signature

cases.derivation: 500000 and 600000 us both at tick 0: a tempo map holds one tempo per tick, and taking either would silently drop the other.
cases.name: two different tempos at one tick

cases.derivation: C4 starts at 0 and again at 480 (83 60) before any note-off, so which note-off ends which note is ambiguous.
cases.name: a second note-on for a sounding pitch

cases.derivation: Format 2 holds independent sequences, each with its own tempo map; the mapping reads one.
cases.name: format 2

cases.derivation: Track 0 plays C4 and track 1 plays D4 (3e), both at 0; a MelodySpec is one melody, so a chooser must name the track (T25) rather than the reader merging or dropping one.
cases.name: notes in two tracks

cases.derivation: C4 on channel 1 (90) and D4 on channel 2 (91) in one track; one melody is one channel.
cases.name: notes on two MIDI channels

cases.derivation: At 1920 PPQ (0780) the note-off at tick 1 is 960 x 1 / 1920 = half a tick; rounding would retime it.
cases.name: a tick that is not a whole 960 PPQ tick

cases.derivation: C4 starts and ends at tick 0; a MelodySpec note lasts at least one tick.
cases.name: a zero-length note

cases.derivation: C4 starts at 0 and the track ends at 960 (87 40 ff 2f 00) with no note-off, so its length is unknown.
cases.name: a note still sounding at End of Track

cases.derivation: The file starts 'RIFF', not 'MThd' (4d 54 68 64).
cases.name: not a MIDI file header

cases.derivation: 0 ticks per quarter note cannot place any event.
cases.name: a division of 0

cases.derivation: Format 0 has exactly one track.
cases.name: format 0 with two tracks

cases.derivation: The first chunk after the header is 'MTrl'; unknown chunks are refused, not skipped.
cases.name: a chunk that is not MTrk

cases.derivation: The chunk says 8 bytes but the file ends after 4.
cases.name: a chunk shorter than its length

cases.derivation: The 9 bytes end after the note-off; ff 2f 00 never comes.
cases.name: a track without End of Track

cases.derivation: A second event follows End of Track inside the chunk.
cases.name: data after End of Track

cases.derivation: One stray byte follows the only chunk.
cases.name: bytes after the last chunk

cases.derivation: 80 80 80 80 still has its continuation bit after four bytes, the SMF maximum.
cases.name: a delta time longer than four bytes

cases.derivation: ff 01 00 (an empty text event) cancels running status, so the data byte 3c at 960 has no status.
cases.name: running status after a meta event

cases.derivation: The note-on's velocity byte is 90, a status byte; data bytes are below 80.
cases.name: a status byte where data belongs

cases.derivation: f8 (timing clock) is a real-time message; a file holds only channel, SysEx and meta events.
cases.name: a system message in a track

cases.derivation: ff 51 must carry 3 bytes; 02 07 a1 carries 2.
cases.name: a tempo event of the wrong length

cases.derivation: C4 sounds from 0 to 1920 and again from 960; one channel cannot hold both, and the first note-off would end the wrong note.
cases.name: two overlapping notes of one pitch

cases.derivation: The tempo list repeats tick 0, so it does not strictly increase (melody.wellformed).
cases.name: two tempos at one tick

cases.derivation: Written as is, a reader would hear the SMF default 4/4 before 960, a meter the MelodySpec never stated.
cases.name: a meter that does not start at tick 0

cases.derivation: The first note-on is 268435456 = 2^28 ticks after 0, one more than the largest four-byte delta time, 0x0fffffff.
cases.name: a gap longer than the SMF delta-time maximum
